prior_range_withdrawn.statement: The H1-CPU prereg bounded the three-policy total between the sealed GPU cloud spend 24.286569 USD and the R0 cloud-only figure 64.64643093818181 USD.
prior_range_withdrawn.why_wrong: That upper bound is one policy's cost. slo_escalate on CPU is about the R0 figure by itself. emission_escalate and full_signal_bounceback still add their GPU costs, because those triggers do not depend on prefill speed. The total is the sum, not a number inside one policy's range.

bootstrap.formula: Resample that policy's escalated entries with replacement. Each draw's per-depth mean cloud_usd is applied to a fixed N(k). A draw with no cloud turn at depth k uses the full-sample mean at k. Cap is the 99.5th percentile. Same procedure as R0 cap v2.

slo_escalate.n_definition: N(k) is every slo_escalate turn at depth k (732 turns). Every cold turn is treated as cloud because CPU prefill exceeds the 10 s SLO inside the 468-token limit measured on 7f232f86.
slo_escalate.cost_source: Pooled cloud turns from the three GPU policies. slo_escalate itself has 0 cloud turns on d482c621, so it has no cloud-cost sample of its own.
slo_escalate.expected_formula: 732 * (sealed cloud_usd 24.286569 / 275 cloud turns) = 64.64643093818181. This is the R0 cloud-only prediction.
slo_escalate.cap_source: R0 cap v2 99.5th percentile, which applies the entry bootstrap's per-depth means to this same N(k). Recorded in derived/h1_hybrid/R0_CAP_V2.json cap_usd.

emission_escalate.n_definition: N(k) is the sealed emission cloud-turn count at depth k. Triggers are a missing tool call, which does not depend on TTFT, so the CPU session is predicted to match the GPU cloud-turn pattern.

full_signal_bounceback.n_definition: N(k) is the sealed bounceback cloud-turn count at depth k. Triggers are no parseable tool call, step budget, or a tool error. Those do not depend on TTFT.

local_only.n_definition: local_only never escalates, so the cloud cost is 0.
